Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Butch Otter]] chose not to run for a fourth term, and the state's primaries were held on May 15.{{cite web|url=http://www.ncsl.org/research/elections-and-campaigns/2018-state-primary-election-dates.aspx|title=2018 State Primary Election Dates|first=National Conference of State|last=Legislatures|website=www.ncsl.org|access-date=May 22, 2018|archive-date=April 20, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420154714/http://www.ncsl.org/research/elections-and-campaigns/2018-state-primary-election-dates.aspx|url-status=dead}} Former state representative [[Paulette Jordan]] was the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]]'s nominee. She was the first Democratic nominee from [[Northern Idaho]] since [[Cecil Andrus]], who was first elected governor in [[1970 Idaho gubernatorial election|1970]]. Had she won, she'd also have been the first female Native American governor of Idaho.{{cite web |last1=Richert |first1=Kevin |title=Democratic Candidates Split on Marijuana Legalization |url=https://www.idahoednews.org/kevins-blog/democratic-candidates-split-on-marijuana-legalization/ |website=Idaho Ed News |date=April 23, 2018 |access-date=February 14, 2019}} Jordan lost to incumbent [[Lieutenant Governor of Idaho|lieutenant governor]] [[Brad Little]] by 21.6 percentage points, for a seventh consecutive Republican victory. A record 605,131 votes were cast for governor in 2018, a 37.6% increase over the previous election in [[Idaho gubernatorial election, 2014|2014]] {{nowrap|(439,830 votes).}} {{nowrap|The previous high}} was 452,535 votes in [[Idaho gubernatorial election, 2010|2010]]. ==Republican primary== Incumbent governor [[Butch Otter]] chose not to run for reelection for a fourth term in office. ===Candidates=== ====Declared==== * Tommy Ahlquist, businessman and former emergency physician{{cite news|last=Dentzer|first=Kevin|title=Ahlquist makes it official: In campaign for governor, he starts 97-town tour this week|url=http://www.idahostatesman.com/news/politics-government/state-politics/article135627508.html|newspaper=[[Idaho Statesman]]|date=February 28, 2017|access-date=March 1, 2017}} * Harley Brown, [[perennial candidate]] * Dalton Cannady * [[Raúl Labrador]], incumbent [[U.S. representative]] from {{ushr|ID|1}}{{cite news|last=Russell|first=Betsy Z.|title=Idaho Rep.
